prompt:
Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Sam and Max together: Sam, the dog detective (a big brown dog in a light blue-gray suit, white shirt, striped dark blue tie and a blue-gray fedora) and Max, the white rabbit-like creature (long ears, wide toothy grin, no clothes). The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (4 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 180 to 248 pixels tall and from 292 to 924 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig041_09/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.


Verified source / identity clarification for this office introduction, costume41 chore6 room7: BOTH Sam and Max occupy the SAME cel. Preserve precisely the first image's pose, silhouettes, crops, size, orientation, relative scale and spacing, even when only fragments are visible. Sam wears the blue-gray suit/fedora, white shirt/cuffs, dark blue/black striped tie, orange brown muzzle/hands/feet. Max is cream-white, long pink-lined ears, tiny black eyes and a broad triangular toothy grin, unclothed. Image2 is Sam identity, image3 Max identity, image4 OUR already painted preceding cels for style/color continuity ONLY; image1 decides the current poses. New art has smooth anti-aliased clean dark outlines and restrained comic shading. Do not propagate the old masters' colored fringe speckles or white matte. Genuine transparent alpha with no background, no halos or glow; not pixel art and not 3D. Preserve source fingers, teeth and small separated pieces. Match all mouth states exactly; Sam never gains a protruding tongue in these cels.
Exactly FOUR cels arranged as in input: one wide cel in row1, one wide cel in row2, then TWO cels in row3, a wide left and a narrow right. Sam curls up, rises from a crouch and lifts Max UP SIDE DOWN in both hands. In the last two cels Max ears hang DOWN, face inverted and feet point UP; do not turn Max upright. Match the original crossing of Sam hands with Max body/head, not an invented grip. A single paper piece drifts far RIGHT in first three cels; in the fourth it is the tiny separate pale piece at lower LEFT of the figures. Keep it. Preserve source mouths; no invented tongue.
Output exact1536x1024 RGBA, all frames at their original positions, true transparent gutters. No numbers, labels, frames, floor, added shadow or decorations. Preserve the colors and twists of the gray-white paper, not new objects.

Precise rotation clarification: source cel3 (lower LEFT) is the IN-BETWEEN rotation, Max head turned roughly sideways, one ear extends LEFT and the other DOWN. Only source cel4 (lower RIGHT) has Max fully inverted with ears hanging DOWN. The original source pose overrides the general upside-down description. Do not skip this intermediate rotation. Sam mouth has the small visible white open mouth in these lower two source cels; preserve that state, NO TONGUE.
